title: Chicken Meal Prep Trays
seoTitle: Chicken Meal Prep Trays | Firefighter Meal
subtitle: Portioned trays, reheat-ready
description: Portioned trays, reheat-ready. Sized for a full crew, with timing that still works when the kitchen gets interrupted.

steps.title: Prep and season
steps.instruction: Cube chicken breasts and sweet potatoes into even 1-inch pieces. Toss chicken, sweet potatoes, and broccoli separately with olive oil, garlic powder, smoked paprika, and salt.

steps.title: Roast in stages
steps.instruction: Spread sweet potatoes on one sheet pan and roast at 425°F for 10 minutes before adding chicken and broccoli to a second pan — sweet potatoes need a head start to cook through.

steps.title: Finish roasting
steps.instruction: Roast both pans another 18–20 minutes, swapping racks halfway, until chicken reads 165°F and vegetables are tender with browned edges.

steps.title: Portion into containers
steps.instruction: Divide cooked rice, roasted chicken, sweet potatoes, and broccoli evenly across meal prep containers — about 1 cup rice and 6 oz chicken per container.

steps.title: Cool and label
steps.instruction: Let containers cool uncovered 15–20 minutes before sealing lids, then refrigerate. Label with the date; reheat covered to 165°F before eating.

proTips: Cool portions in shallow trays before the fridge — deep containers stay in the danger zone too long.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold plates after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Meal Prep Trays with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Meal Prep Trays on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Portion into individual containers on night one — locker-friendly for shift two.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Portioned trays, reheat-ready. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
mealPrepNotes: Cook boneless chicken thighs and sauce ahead; assemble day-of in under 20 minutes. Label and date everything in the fridge.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
